results.psh_output: Injected on the 3rd ProcessLauncher.launch of 'sleep 30 | echo hi | cat' (in-process Shell, PSH_STRICT_ERRORS=1). [A: OSError] outcome: run_command returned rc=1 (stderr 'psh: line 1: <command>:1: unexpected error: [Errno 24] injected EMFILE'); fds leaked in parent: {}; member#1 ECHILD (already reaped); member#2 ECHILD (already reaped). [B: RuntimeError] outcome: EXCEPTION RuntimeError: injected non-OSError; fds leaked in parent: {3: 'fifo', 4: 'fifo', 6: 'fifo'}; member#1 pid RUNNING (waitpid WNOHANG -> (0,0)); member#2 RUNNING; after closing leaked fds: member#1 still RUNNING (sleep 30), member#2 exited, reaped now: status=13.
results.note: Confirmed by fault injection (scratch c126_inject.py monkeypatching shell.process_launcher.launch). With an OSError (inside `except (OSError, ValueError)` at pipeline.py:344) the rollback works: no fds leaked, both forked members SIGKILLed and reaped. With a RuntimeError the rollback is skipped: three FIFO fds leak in the parent (sync pipe r/w + the carried boundary read end), the leader keeps running, and member#2 (`echo hi`, which would exit instantly if released) stays blocked on the sync-pipe read — it only ran/exited (SIGPIPE, its consumer was never forked) once the harness closed the leaked fds. Code argument from #23 holds at HEAD; no in-shell trigger constructed (launch() itself documents only OSError), so this remains an unproven-from-the-shell defensive gap.
